channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-05
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 97 news received.

item.title: Meta changes the names of its artificial intelligence models
item.description: Meta has made an important decision about how it names its AI models. Charles Rollet details the change.

item.title: Elon Musk spent 446 million dollars supporting Republicans
item.description: Elon Musk spent 446 million dollars supporting the Republican Party, including 224 million dollars in Texas, which turned Democratic. Tesla and SpaceX shares finished lower on Wednesday.

item.title: Voters oppose new AI infrastructure in their region
item.description: According to an NBC News exit poll, a majority of voters believe AI and data centers played an important role in their vote. They also said they oppose new AI infrastructure in their community.

item.title: Cat Wu joins OpenAI after leaving Anthropic
item.description: The former head of Claude Code product will now lead core product management at OpenAI. Her hiring is a major win for OpenAI ahead of Anthropic’s expected IPO.

item.title: The AI boom is turning fiber-optic cables into coveted assets
item.description: The artificial intelligence boom is making fiber-optic cables particularly sought-after materials.

item.title: Google disables Gemini and AI Search by default in schools
item.description: Google has finally made Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search disabled by default for schools, following controversy over the inability to turn off certain AI features without losing Search. DuckDuckGo published instructions for changing the default search engine and accused Google of imposing AI on children.

item.title: OpenAI launches Images 2.6, 50% faster and able to create GIFs
item.description: Images 2.6 is arriving in ChatGPT, Codex and the API with GIF generation, saved references to preserve a character’s appearance, image labeling, SVG export and a complexity setting. OpenAI says generation is about 50% faster.

item.title: OpenAI plans to acquire code-hosting startup Pierre
item.description: OpenAI has agreed to acquire Pierre Computer, the startup that already hosts Codex code repositories. The deal brings OpenAI closer to GitHub’s territory.

item.title: Chris Lehane presents OpenAI’s 2028 policy agenda
item.description: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane presented a 2028 policy program focused on workers, education, safety and data centers.

item.title: An open tissue atlas aims to improve AI against cancer
item.description: Scientists at EPFL created spora, described as the largest open collection of tissue images, to help artificial intelligence better understand cancer.

item.title: Switzerland bets on open, sovereign AI against tech giants
item.description: Facing the dominance of American and Chinese artificial intelligence giants, Switzerland is betting on open, sovereign AI.

item.title: Swiss people are using AI extensively to interpret their symptoms
item.description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming part of Swiss healthcare habits, according to the CSS study on the subject.

item.title: ChatGPT Reaches 20% of Google’s Search Volume
item.description: According to Adam Fry of OpenAI, ChatGPT now handles approximately one-fifth of the number of search-like queries handled by Google. ChatGPT would therefore be ahead of Bing, which holds about 5% of the search market.

item.title: SpaceX Chooses Qualcomm to Build Starlink’s 5G Network
item.description: SpaceX has hired Qualcomm to build a terrestrial 5G network for Starlink Mobile, with base stations to be deployed in the United States starting in 2027. The agreement covers tens of thousands of sites using Qualcomm’s Dragonwing platform.

item.title: Anthropic Is Working on a System to Prove AI Model Identity
item.description: Anthropic is developing a system intended to prove the identity of artificial intelligence models.

item.title: Valve Changes Steam Publishing Rules Amid Influx of AI Games
item.description: Valve has changed its Steam publishing rules as the platform faces an influx of games using artificial intelligence.

item.title: Meta Seeks to Raise Up to $25 Billion in Debt to Fund AI
item.description: Meta is seeking to raise up to $25 billion in the debt markets as its artificial intelligence spending increases.

item.title: Netflix Tests an AI-Powered Discover Tab to Recommend Content
item.description: Netflix’s new Discover tab uses artificial intelligence to help users find a program based on their mood.

item.title: Advice for a Tesla Model 3 Battery Nearing the End of Its Warranty
item.description: A Tesla Model 3’s long-range battery is reaching the end of its eight-year warranty. The owner asks whether they should keep driving it as is or take any specific measures.

item.title: Buying a Used Tesla Model Y from an Independent Dealer
item.description: A buyer is looking for a 2022 or 2023 Model Y Long Range AWD, with a clean title and between 30,000 and 40,000 miles. They are asking for advice from people who bought their Tesla from a third-party dealer.

item.title: Climate Control Error on a 2019 Tesla Model 3 Performance
item.description: An owner reports the “VCFRONT_a160_compressorInhibited” and “lowSuctionPressure” errors. One response distinguishes a transient error, which may disappear when conditions change, from a genuine problem, particularly one caused by insufficient refrigerant.

item.title: The blue wave puts tech’s right wing on the defensive
item.description: The 2026 midterm elections dealt a major public setback to a technology industry that had moved closer to Republicans. The infrastructure needed for AI’s future, particularly data centers, is at the heart of the backlash.

item.title: A small North Dakota town supports data centers
item.description: A small North Dakota town is the only place described as having voted in favor of data centers.

item.title: Neocloud stocks fall after the U.S. elections
item.description: Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren fell, while the technology sector overall ended the session higher. A slowdown among AI companies could nevertheless reduce the risk of supply exceeding demand.

item.title: California’s billionaire wealth tax is in trouble
item.description: Early results from Proposition 40 show a clear lead for the “no” vote. The final count is not yet known.

item.title: U.S. futures are mixed ahead of the jobs report
item.description: U.S. stock futures were moving in different directions on Thursday. Investors are assessing the post-election rebound ahead of Friday’s jobs report.

item.title: A rare recession indicator has flashed
item.description: The S&P 500’s forward price-to-earnings ratio, an indicator that has historically appeared around recessions, has fallen sharply. In most years when this ratio dropped significantly, the United States was in a recession or a bear market.

item.title: The skills that matter most on Wall Street in the AI era
item.description: AI is changing the qualities that help people stand out when starting on Wall Street. Business Insider’s Rising Stars explain which skills to develop as AI automates an increasing share of the work.

item.title: The blue wave could benefit markets through political gridlock
item.description: Democratic victories in Congress could create political gridlock that has historically been favorable to markets. They will also affect AI-related stocks, the war in Iran and the deficit.

item.title: Robots are transforming the work of Ukrainian frontline soldiers
item.description: Robots now perform tasks that previously exposed soldiers to danger, such as transporting ammunition or evacuating troops from the combat zone. Several Ukrainian service members describe a war that is becoming increasingly robotic.

item.title: Delays threaten Microsoft’s AI data-center partners
item.description: Microsoft cut its annual capital-spending forecast by 5 billion dollars, with its CFO citing delays at third-party cloud providers, among other factors. Satellite analysis suggests that two data-center projects could be affected.

item.title: Executives are beginning to regret forcing AI on their employees
item.description: After pushing employees to adopt AI, executives are confronting an abundance of bland, low-quality content resulting from their own policies.

item.title: Canva offers support to more than 1,200 laid-off employees
item.description: Canva is offering more than 1,200 departing employees interview preparation, LinkedIn Premium, access to its network and the opportunity to apply for 10,000-dollar grants to start a startup. Verizon and Chevron have also introduced reskilling programs.

item.title: Good Good’s former marketing director sues the company for defamation
item.description: Jeff Lefkovits, Good Good’s former marketing director, claims he was made a scapegoat after the advertising fiasco. He is seeking more than 1 million dollars from the company and its former executive.

item.title: The nanny killed in the Learjet crash had a degree in biomedical engineering
item.description: The nanny who died in the Learjet crash had earned a degree in biomedical engineering.

item.title: Grocery retailers oppose the DoorDash–Instacart deal
item.description: Food retailers are challenging the agreement reached between DoorDash and Instacart.

item.title: Seasonal retail jobs are leaving store floors
item.description: Temporary holiday-season jobs are gradually moving away from the sales floor.

item.title: Zohran Mamdani’s pied-à-terre tax clears a legal hurdle
item.description: The pied-à-terre tax backed by New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani won an important victory in court.

item.title: Barry Diller advises Hollywood to stop chasing Netflix
item.description: Barry Diller believes Hollywood should stop trying to imitate or catch up with Netflix.

item.title: The Learjet crash prompts public figures to rethink private aviation
item.description: The fatal Learjet crash is prompting some wealthy public figures to reconsider traveling by private jet.

item.title: Elon Musk deleted his message urging people to vote Republican
item.description: The “vote red” message posted by Elon Musk disappeared after Election Day.

item.title: Uber’s AI agents booked only four rides during Halloween
item.description: During Halloween week, AI agents booked only four Uber rides and around 500 food orders, out of roughly 320 million rides and orders. The CEO believes adoption remains very limited, in part because booking manually takes about 50 seconds.

item.title: Meta acquires Conductor, a specialist in coordinating coding agents
item.description: Meta acquired Conductor, a startup whose interface directs multiple programming agents simultaneously. Its hosted service is scheduled to shut down on November 20.

item.title: AI-linked PACs spend millions in the midterms
item.description: AI-focused political action committees spent millions during the midterm elections, with mixed results. They spent 4.8 million dollars on a South Carolina Senate candidate who lost, among other expenditures.

item.title: Nothing will launch an AI product without a new screen in December
item.description: Nothing CEO Carl Pei announced that the company’s first product designed natively around AI would launch in December. He said it would not have a new screen.

item.title: Asian AI-related stocks plunge
item.description: Asian AI-related stocks fell, with SoftBank down 5.3%, Tokyo Electron down 7.7% and Advantest down 9.4%.

item.title: Moonshot releases the open weights of its Kimi K3.1 Pro model
item.description: Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro with open, downloadable weights, text and image understanding, and a one-million-token memory. The model is distributed under a custom license and can be tried on HuggingChat.

item.title: Apple opens the Apple Intelligence developer beta in China
item.description: Apple opened an Apple Intelligence developer beta in China featuring Writing Tools, Genmoji and a version of Siri powered by Qwen. A public release is planned for December.

item.title: True leaders need champions and partners
item.description: The editorial argues that true leaders do not need consultants, but champions and partners.

item.title: The Lake Geneva region surpasses Zurich in economic clout
item.description: According to new estimates from the Swiss Federal Statistical Office, Switzerland’s economic map has been redrawn, with the Lake Geneva region now surpassing Zurich in economic clout.

item.title: Scientific debate over AI consciousness intensifies
item.description: The possibility that artificial intelligences may one day possess a form of consciousness is the subject of growing scientific debate.

item.title: Ancient retroviruses may have differentiated human and chimpanzee brains
item.description: Retroviral infections occurring millions of years ago may have contributed to differentiating human and chimpanzee brains.

item.title: Brain–machine interface reveals consciousness in unresponsive patients
item.description: In intensive-care patients with acute brain injuries who were clinically unable to respond, a brain–machine interface revealed hidden consciousness.

item.title: Japan performs first post-approval iPS cell transplant for Parkinson’s
item.description: Japan has carried out its first post-approval iPS cell transplant as part of the treatment of Parkinson’s disease.

item.title: LHC collides oxygen to study the early Universe
item.description: CERN’s Large Hadron Collider has carried out oxygen collisions for the first time to probe the Universe’s earliest moments.

item.title: An AI Website Model with Dual Interfaces for Humans and Agents
item.description: A new study conducted with Knotch proposes websites with two surfaces: an intent-responsive interface for humans and a service-oriented semantic interface for agents. Both would rely on a shared brand context model capable of keeping the company’s content, rules, and capabilities up to date.

item.title: Apple Opens Siri’s AI to All Apps
item.description: Apple now allows app developers to integrate their content and actions with Siri through a developer preview. Integrations could include checking a delivery, booking a service, or combining multiple actions.

item.title: Nvidia Will Be Able to Fulfill Only 1% of Chinese GPU Orders
item.description: Over the coming months, Nvidia will deliver only about 1% of the RTX Pro 5500 GPUs ordered by Chinese companies such as ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent. Demand reportedly amounts to about $70 billion, far exceeding current production capacity.

item.title: Revolut Cuts AI Coding Costs Tenfold by Dropping Claude
item.description: UK fintech Revolut is reducing its AI-related coding costs by eliminating Claude and hosting its models itself.

item.title: Google Expands Voluntary Buyouts to Reduce Its Workforce
item.description: Google is expanding its voluntary departure programs to reduce its workforce without carrying out layoffs.

item.title: Apple Explicitly Bans the Use of Confidential Information in Prediction Markets
item.description: Apple now explicitly prohibits employees from using confidential information in prediction markets.

item.title: Data Centers Turn to Former Jet Engines to Generate Power
item.description: Data centers are using former jet engines as power-access wait times grow longer.

item.title: Hackers Used Fake Job Interviews in a $6.3 Billion Heist
item.description: Hackers used fake job interviews to organize a $6.3 billion theft targeting Binance.

item.title: Neuralink’s Chinese rival targets obesity with an electronic GLP-1
item.description: Neuralink’s Chinese rival is seeking to treat obesity with an electronic GLP-1 treatment.

item.title: Microsoft Reveals Its Plan to Avoid a Windows 11 RAM Crisis
item.description: Microsoft is preparing a plan intended to avoid Windows 11 RAM problems.

item.title: Canva Cuts Jobs, Affecting 22% of Its Workforce
item.description: Canva’s first layoffs affect 22% of its staff, in what the company describes as its most difficult moment.

item.title: The SaaS Apocalypse Began in October
item.description: The article claims that the software-as-a-service apocalypse began in October.

item.title: Oracle Abandons $7 Billion Deal with Tencent
item.description: Oracle is abandoning a $7 billion deal with Tencent under pressure from the Trump administration.

item.title: AI medical assistants sometimes access unnecessary identifiers
item.description: AI medical assistants sometimes access patient identifiers they do not need. Checking permissions before the task nearly eliminated these unnecessary accesses.

item.title: Gender influences AI’s automated candidate evaluations
item.description: A study shows that simply indicating a candidate’s gender changes approval rates by up to 1.7 points and reverses up to 3.3% of decisions.

item.title: Trust in national news media rises in the United States
item.description: American adults’ trust in national news media rose by six points in one year, to 62%. Trust in social media news remained stable at 38%, according to a Pew survey.

item.title: What an AI agent actually does
item.description: The chapter explains the difference between an AI that responds and one that acts, as well as the reliability of multistep tasks. It also shows which actions an agent can perform alone and which require human approval.

item.title: Connecting AI to the tools you already use
item.description: The chapter explains what connecting AI to a tool enables compared with sending files case by case. It helps identify the risks, protection settings and first system to connect.

item.title: Texas turns Democratic, to the dismay of tech entrepreneurs
item.description: Texas shifted to the Democratic camp, disappointing entrepreneurs in the technology sector.

item.title: A Cybercab spotted near Florida Mall
item.description: A forum member says they found a Cybercab where route 417 meets World Drive, near Disney World. They list the next stops on its route, including a Marriott, I-4 and Disney World.

item.title: A Tesla’s tire pressure system stops working
item.description: A member reports that tire pressure is no longer displayed. A response explains that in the United States, regulations require a tire-pressure monitoring system, but not necessarily sensors, and that software monitoring of wheel behavior may be sufficient.

item.title: Trading Tesla referral codes for free FSD access
item.description: The discussion concerns the terms of use for Tesla referral codes, including a possible limit of 12 referrals per calendar year and the 48-month period mentioned by some members.

item.title: A Tesla owner considers a Rivian R2 for someone close to him
item.description: A close friend approaching retirement has long appreciated efficient electric vehicles but has never bought one. He is familiar with the member’s Teslas but has not yet taken the plunge.

item.title: Is the FSD price prorated mid-month?
item.description: A member asks how much a mid-month FSD subscription would cost for an upcoming trip, after a previous subscription expired.

item.title: Rear-impact repair estimated at nearly 4,000 dollars
item.description: Tesla and the insurance adjuster both estimated the repair at just under 4,000 dollars. The proposed solution is to straighten the dent, which does not fully convince the owner.

item.title: A Tesla’s windshield wipers skip across the glass
item.description: A member says they have not experienced this problem but believes it could come from the entire wiper arm assembly, which may be defective or have another fault.

item.title: At Orbia, employees present their own ideas to the CEO
item.description: At Orbia, the innovation team stays in the background so that employees who originated the ideas can present the results themselves and receive the credit. This rule contributes to a 75% engagement rate, compared with about 30% on average.

item.title: An innovation culture built by 1.25 people at the NHS
item.description: At Clatterbridge Cancer Centre, two people representing a combined 1.25 full-time equivalents created a system for collecting staff ideas and acting quickly. Their approach includes a dedicated ideas space, 30-minute “Time to Think” sessions and an accelerated governance pathway.

item.title: RBI rethinks its innovation program despite a 9.3 out of 10 rating
item.description: Raiffeisen Bank International’s Innovation School was viewed very positively by 92% of participants, but only 41% felt six months later that they had achieved their learning goal. The team applied design thinking to its own program and made four changes as a result.

item.title: Why most employees think innovation is not their job
item.description: Linda Hill of Harvard Business School explains that presenting innovation as an activity reserved for technologists alienates other employees. She suggests defining innovation as any useful novelty and connecting everyone’s daily work to the company’s mission.

item.title: Captain Picard’s final leadership lesson
item.description: While watching the final scene of Star Trek: The Next Generation, Bob Gilbreath rediscovers a leadership lesson: do not wait until the end to appreciate and support team members. Leaders must be authentic and present with their employees.

item.title: Snowflake unveils AI agents that work after you disconnect
item.description: Snowflake announced CoCo and CoWork Bots, agents under development that can handle tasks in the background and ask a human for help when needed. Recurring automations and planned integrations with Slack, spreadsheets and mobile devices were also announced.

item.title: Suspected Cyberattacks Destroy Food in European Supermarkets
item.description: More than 40 supermarkets across seven countries were affected by suspected attacks that remotely raised the temperature of refrigeration systems, destroying food. The incidents highlight the exposure of connected operational equipment whose software may no longer be supported.

item.title: Does AI save time or make work take longer?
item.description: The latest ActivTrak research links intensive AI use to longer workdays, shorter focus periods and more app switching. Differences between the samples and measurement limitations make the results difficult to compare.

item.title: Hasty AI-related layoffs could make rehiring costly
item.description: Gartner predicts that 30% of employees replaced by AI will be rehired by 2029, probably at a higher cost. The firm recommends assessing how work is changing before deciding which positions to eliminate.

item.title: Snowflake centralizes controls for enterprise AI agents
item.description: Snowflake’s Cortex AI Gateway, now available, centralizes policies governing agent connections, model access and spending. Business Ontology will let agents use approved definitions of business concepts, while sandbox execution and abuse detection remain in private preview.

item.title: Bull and Schwarz Digits plan sovereign European AI infrastructure
item.description: Bull and Schwarz Digits have signed an agreement to develop AI infrastructure for European organizations in regulated and strategic sectors. The planned architecture combines European cloud STACKIT with Bull’s computing hardware, liquid cooling and AI software.

item.title: National Grid plans major substation for data center expansion
item.description: National Grid plans a major substation in Teesside to supply a data center, battery storage and other electricity-intensive industries. Its initial capacity of 1,440 MVA is due to come online by the end of 2029.

item.title: CIO survey reveals gap between AI deployment and readiness
item.description: An Accenture survey of 300 technology leaders finds that 64% are accelerating enterprise AI deployment, but only 7% are optimizing it at scale. Adoption and user training are the main obstacles, and nearly half of companies still require manual approvals for IT operations agents.

item.title: UK businesses near deadline for migration to digital telephony
item.description: Openreach says about 300,000 copper business lines remain active ahead of the January deadline. They include connections used by payment terminals, alarms and building systems.

item.title: AI agents expected to drive a 55% increase in identity spending
item.description: Juniper Research forecasts that global spending on identity and access management will rise from 26.2 billion dollars in 2026 to 40.5 billion in 2031. The increase is driven by the growing number of AI agents and other nonhuman identities.

item.title: Responsibility for AI agents is still missing from organizational charts
item.description: A Gravitee survey finds that 85% of executives are under pressure to deploy more agents, while about 80% are concerned about their security and only 7% have appointed responsible owners. According to Rory Blundell, the challenge is more about governance and organizational accountability than technology itself.
